answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding each identity to one live-verified human. Enrollment needs a scan matched against every prior one, so one face or iris mints one credential and a second pass is refused. The body is the scarce resource: it cannot whisper one person's uniqueness into a thousand accounts. A sybil wanting a thousand identities must field a thousand people; like a karst's separate caves, none berth twice at the wharf. Assumes an honest issuer that dedups globally and spoof-resistant scans; a rich attacker can hire people, so it blocks cheap minting, not wealth.
